inputs.fcf_normalization_note: FY2025 GAAP FCF (OCF 7,408 - capex 2,112 = 5,296) is depressed by the fairlife contingent-consideration settlement: total liability 6,173 paid March 2025 (Q2-2026 10-Q MD&A, other operating charges), of which ~6,100 ran through operating activities (Q1-2025 OCF was -5,202 against +528 a year earlier and +2,021 in Q1-2026). reported_fcf is restated ex that payment (~11,396). FY2024 GAAP FCF 4,741 is likewise depressed by the 6,000 IRS Tax Litigation Deposit paid 2024-09-10, which sits in other noncurrent assets, not in cash. H1-2026 clean FCF was 6,859 (OCF 7,543 - capex 684).
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash flow statement stock-based compensation add-back (XBRL ShareBasedCompensation 279); withholding on net-share settlement is not tagged and KO publishes no combined figure; at 0.58% of revenue the omission is immaterial
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 treasury purchases 746 (10-K); H1-2026 663 for 7.3m shares. Buybacks roughly offset SBC issuance so the flat count is funded, not a convention
inputs.share_count_basis: Weighted-average diluted shares 4,313m for Q2-2026 (10-Q for period ended 2026-07-03); basic 4,303m; dei cover-page count 4,302.5m at 2026-04-28. Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows (charging both would double-count)
inputs.balance_sheet_note: Q2-2026 10-Q (period ended 2026-07-03, filed 2026-07-29, accession 0001628280-26-050503): cash 12,907; short-term investments 622; marketable securities 2,842; loans and notes payable 48 + current maturities 6,494 + long-term debt 37,001 = 43,543 total debt; NCI 2,165; equity-method investments carrying 20,782. This filing is NOT in the SEC companyfacts XBRL API nor in KO_Metrics.csv as of 2026-09-29; the CSV row labelled 'Q2 2026' (revenue 12,472) is actually the quarter ended 2026-04-03, i.e. Q1-2026 (KO 52/53-week quarter; the XBRL fy/fp says 2026 Q1). Anchors here were read from the 10-Q HTML directly.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows discounted at a USD WACC: 10-yr UST ~4.2%, ERP 5.0%, beta ~0.6 (consumer staple) gives cost of equity ~7.2%; pre-tax cost of debt ~4.3% (FY2025 interest expense 1,654 on ~44bn debt is 3.8%; marginal issuance higher), after-tax ~3.4%; market-value weights ~92% equity / 8% debt give 6.9%, rounded to 7.0%. Same WACC in all three scenarios: risk is charged in the flows and the weights, not the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP filer; operating lease cost is inside SG&A and therefore inside EBITDA, so leases are already an operating cost in the flows. Lease liabilities (~1.5bn) are excluded from net debt. One treatment, not two.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated (Bottling Investments includes partly-owned bottlers), so the noncontrolling interest of 2,165 (Q2-2026 balance sheet) is deducted once in the equity bridge; no leakage is charged in the flows.
inputs.non_operating_assets_note: The component build starts from operating income, which EXCLUDES equity income from KO's minority bottler stakes (2,031 in FY2025; 988 in H1-2026 -- CCEP, Coca-Cola FEMSA, Coca-Cola HBC, Coca-Cola Consolidated, Monster and others) and excludes interest income (786 in FY2025). Under the matching-asset rule those stakes go into the bridge at quoted market value (34,286 for the publicly traded investees per the FY2025 10-K, versus total equity-method carrying value 20,235 at FY2025 / 20,782 at Q2-2026 -- the unlisted remainder is left OUT, a deliberate margin of safety) and the cash that earns the interest income is in net debt. Short-term investments and AFS marketable securities are added as cash-equivalents.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row 'operating company, consumer'); first valuation of this ticker, no memory entry. Coca-Cola is an asset-light concentrate business with a stable, mature cash-flow stream -- the standard engine applies, plus the adaptations for non-operating assets (bottler stakes at fair value) and NCI. Owner FCF base 11,117 = normalized reported FCF 11,396 - SBC 279 - interest income 0 (KO carries 30.6bn net debt, so the interest-income strip does not apply; the EBITDA-based forward build excludes it anyway). EBITDA in this build is operating income + D&A on a GAAP basis; FY2025 was 14,812 (30.9%) including the 960 BODYARMOR trademark impairment and ~1.0bn of intangible impairments in total, or ~33.1% ex-impairments; H1-2026 was 37.0% (seasonally the strong half; H1-2025 was 35.9%). The margin paths therefore start at 33% and carry a permanent allowance for the 'other operating charges' KO has booked every year for a decade rather than the company's comparable ~31-33% operating margin plus D&A. Working-capital capture is 0: receivables + inventory roughly equal payables + accrued, so growth neither consumes nor releases cash materially. 10-year horizon because the terminal cap binds at 20x and the paths are near-flat by year 5. Gordon at 7%/2.5% would be 22.8x owner FCF, so the 20x cap binds in the base case; KO trades at ~34x normalized owner FCF (price 87.18 x 4,313 = 376bn market cap; EV ~407bn), which is why the house value sits well below the price -- the market is paying a bond-proxy multiple that the house method deliberately does not extrapolate.

equity_bridge.item: Publicly traded equity-method bottler investees at quoted market value
equity_bridge.note: FY2025 10-K, XBRL EquityMethodInvestmentQuotedMarketValue 34,286 at 2025-12-31 (28,740 at 2024-12-31). Total equity-method carrying value 20,782 at 2026-07-03; the unlisted investees are excluded. Their equity income (2,031 FY2025) is not in the flows.
Q2-2026 10-Q, equity attributable to NCI; flows are consolidated so NCI is deducted once here

Q2-2026 10-Q Note (Income Taxes): 6.0bn deposit + 514m accrued interest (in other noncurrent assets, NOT in cash) refunded if KO prevails; ~14bn potential incremental tax and interest for 2010-2025 at 2025-12-31, accruing ~0.9bn per half-year, if the Tax Court methodology is upheld. 11th Circuit heard the appeal 2026-06-25 (8th Circuit's Oct-2025 3M reversal on blocked income supports KO). Weighted at 55% win / 45% lose: 0.55 x 6.5 - 0.45 x 15.0 = -3.2bn. The ongoing ETR uplift in a loss is carried in the bear cash-tax path, not here.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: FY2026 guidance (organic ~5%, raised July 2026; Street reported ~4%) cross-checked against the 3-yr revenue CAGR of 3.7% and the 5.5-6.6% owner-FCF CAGRs; equity CAGR rejected as the anchor (see divergence warning)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (~10%) diverges >30% from revenue CAGR (3.7% 3-yr). KO pays out ~75% of earnings as dividends, so book growth is driven by AOCI/FX and the FY2025 earnings jump (net income 13,137 vs 10,649, as FY2024 carried ~3bn of impairments and refranchising losses), not by reinvestment. EPS CAGRs (11%) are likewise flattered by the FY2024 trough and by FY2020's COVID base. Neither is a forward growth rate for a business guiding 4-6% long-term organic revenue growth.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs use the owner-FCF series (reported FCF normalized for the 2024 IRS deposit and 2025 fairlife payment, less SBC): FY2020 8,526; FY2021 10,921; FY2022 9,173; FY2023 9,493; FY2024 10,455; FY2025 11,117. The GAAP reported-FCF CAGRs (-17.8% 3-yr, -9.4% 5-yr) are meaningless because of the two ~6bn one-offs; they are recorded so a reader sees the gap. SBC has been flat at ~0.6% of revenue for a decade, so SBC growth does not distort the owner series.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 +5% reported: H1-2026 revenue 25,852 was +9.2% (Q1 carried six extra days that Q4 gives back; Q2 +6.7%), organic guided ~5%, modest FX tailwind, bottler-refranchising structural drag; thereafter 4% fading to 2.5% -- KO's long-term algorithm is 4-6% organic and the developed-market CSD volume base is flat, so growth is price/mix plus emerging-market volume.
base.margin_rationale: GAAP EBITDA (op income + D&A) 33.1% in FY2025 ex-impairments and 37.0% in the seasonally strong H1-2026 (+1.1pp YoY). 33% for FY2026 keeps ~1pp of annual 'other operating charges'; drifts to 34% as fairlife/Costa scale and refranchising lifts the concentrate mix. Comparable operating margin guidance implies more, but the house build charges the recurring one-offs.
base.tax_rationale: Cash taxes 2,873 in FY2025 on ~14bn of operating pre-tax (equity income is largely untaxed at KO's level) is ~20%; Pillar Two and the OBBBA push the underlying rate toward 21%.
base.capex_rationale: 4.4% of revenue in FY2024-25 (2,064 / 2,112), heavier than the ~3.5% of a decade ago because of fairlife and Bottling Investments capacity; eases to 4.0% as those projects complete.

bull.rationale: Top of the long-term algorithm sustained: zero-sugar and fairlife carry volume, price/mix holds at 3-4%, emerging-market per-capita growth continues, AI-led RGM and supply-chain productivity add ~2.5pp of margin over five years. Cap 22x reflects a mature compounder the market has historically paid 25x+ for.

bear.rationale: H1-2026 momentum is already banked so FY2026 still grows 3.5%, then GLP-1 adoption and doubled sugar taxes (Mexico IEPS +87% and now on zero-sugar) cap volume while pricing elasticity bites; BODYARMOR-style impairments and restructuring recur, taking EBITDA margin back to 30% (the FY2019-21 GAAP level). Cash tax rises to 24% as the IRS Tax Court methodology is applied prospectively (the 10-Q says it would lift the ETR by low single digits) on top of Pillar Two. Cap 17x for a business growing 1%.

scenario_narratives.base: Coca-Cola remains the world's dominant NARTD franchise and grows revenue 4-5% near term, fading to 2.5%, on price/mix plus emerging-market volume; Coca-Cola Zero Sugar offsets full-sugar decline in developed markets; fairlife and Costa keep the finished-goods mix growing. GAAP EBITDA margin holds 33-34% with ~1pp/yr of recurring 'other operating charges'. The bottler stakes are worth their quoted 34bn and the IRS appeal resolves as a modest net cost. Value is set by a 20x cap on year-10 owner FCF at a 7% WACC -- the market is paying ~34x today.
scenario_narratives.bull: New CEO Braun's technology-led RGM and productivity programme lifts EBITDA margin ~2.5pp to 35.5% while zero-sugar, fairlife and emerging markets keep organic growth at 5-6% for five years; Mexico and other sugar taxes prove absorbable through reformulation; the 11th Circuit reverses the Tax Court (already carried in the bridge weighting) and the 22x cap credits a mature compounder that has historically commanded a premium multiple.
scenario_narratives.bear: GLP-1 uptake (users cut sugary-drink consumption by up to ~65%) and proliferating sugar/packaging taxes structurally cap volume; pricing elasticity ends the price/mix run; sports drinks keep losing to Gatorade with further BODYARMOR write-downs; growth drops to 1% and GAAP EBITDA margin falls back to 30%. The IRS methodology is upheld and applied going forward, adding ~3pp to the cash tax rate on top of the 15bn in the bridge. A 1%-growth staple is capped at 17x.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Symmetric 25/50/25 rather than the 15/50/35 house default. Bull is trimmed because it needs three independent things (sustained 5%+ organic growth, 2.5pp of margin, and a premium exit multiple) to go right for a business already at the top of its long-term algorithm. Bear is raised because the two structural threats -- GLP-1 and the global sugar-tax wave -- are already visible in the data and the IRS outcome is binary; but there is no going-concern, covenant or single-customer risk, so it stays at 25%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: House owner-FCF basis: SBC expensed (small at 0.6% of revenue), share count flat, equity income stripped from the flows and the bottler stakes added at quoted market value, NCI deducted once, the IRS case carried at expected value in the bridge, terminal value capped at 20x owner FCF. Coca-Cola's cash flow is among the most predictable in the market, so the valuation question is almost entirely the multiple: at 7% WACC and a 20x cap the house value is far below a price that embeds ~34x normalized owner FCF and a ~2.9% FCF yield. The house/street band is negligible because SBC is tiny; the gap to the price is a multiple gap, not an accounting-regime gap.
key_risks_to_valuation: IRS transfer-pricing appeal (11th Circuit, argued 2026-06-25): a loss costs the 6.5bn deposit plus ~15bn incremental and raises the go-forward tax rate; a win returns 6.5bn. Carried at -3.2bn expected value; the swing between outcomes is ~5/share.
GLP-1 adoption and sugar taxes (Mexico IEPS doubled in 2026 and extended to zero-sugar) could push developed- and Latin-market volume negative faster than price/mix can offset.
The 20x terminal cap is the single largest driver: Gordon at 7%/2.5% would be 22.8x and the market pays ~34x; every 1x on the cap is worth ~3.5/share.
Bottler stakes are valued at quoted market prices (34.3bn), which move with the investees' own multiples; carrying value is 20.8bn.
FX: most revenue is non-USD; a strong dollar cuts reported growth 2-4pp in bad years and the WACC is USD-built.
Recurring 'one-off' charges: BODYARMOR (960 in FY2025, 760 in FY2024) shows past M&A can be written down again; the margin paths allow ~1pp/yr but a fairlife-scale miss would exceed it.
The Q2-2026 10-Q is missing from the XBRL feed and the CSV mislabels Q1-2026 as Q2-2026; anchors here were read from the filing HTML and should be re-checked once the pipeline ingests it.
